beats.narration_text: The Samsung case matters because it's public and it's damning. April 2023. Engineers were given permission to use ChatGPT at work. Within twenty days, they had leaked internal semiconductor source code three separate times — pasted into ChatGPT to check bugs, to fix defects, and one time they uploaded a recording of an internal meeting. Samsung banned ChatGPT company-wide and opened disciplinary investigations. That's the ceiling on what goes wrong.

Here's the mechanism. On personal Claude plans — Free, Pro, Max — Anthropic's terms allow your chats and coding sessions to be used to improve the model by default. Leave that on, and they can keep your conversations for up to five years. Every piece of confidential company information you paste in sits in that pool. The fix is one toggle, and you need to flip it before the next conversation you have.

beats.narration_text: For Claude: Settings → Privacy → turn off Help improve our AI models. For ChatGPT: Settings → Data controls → turn off Improve the model for everyone. Grok: profile, settings, data controls, turn off everything. Gemini is harder — you navigate to myactivity.google.com and turn off the Gemini activity toggle directly. Important caveat One additional guide covers: the opt-out only applies going forward. Data already in a training run can't be pulled back. Flip the switch now, not after your next session.

the not a lawyer — he's clear about that. But the cases are public. Pasting confidential company information into a personal AI account can be framed three ways by a lawyer: breach of the NDA you signed, because the AI company is an outside party. Violation of data protection laws, depending on jurisdiction. Breach of IT security policy. All three have precedent. The risk isn't hypothetical. It's already happened, and companies have opened investigations over it.

The practical solution, if your company won't pay for an enterprise AI account: keep your personal account, but run a clean-room policy for yourself. Never paste client names, internal financials, source code, or meeting recordings. Anonymize before you paste — replace proper nouns with placeholders. And turn off training, as covered. If you're the one managing risk for a team, the advice is the same: flag the legal exposure and advocate for an enterprise plan. Enterprise plans don't train on your data at all.
